Where it began

Shimron Hetmyer was born on 26 December 1996 in East Berbice-Corentyne, in Guyana. He made his name early. In 2016, aged 19, he captained the West Indies at the Under-19 World Cup in Bangladesh, made two half-centuries along the way and lifted the trophy after his side beat India in the final.

That same year he made his first appearance in Twenty20 cricket for the Guyana Amazon Warriors in the Caribbean Premier League, the start of a long association with his home franchise.

The player

His Test debut came against Pakistan in April 2017, and he played 16 Tests for the West Indies between 2017 and 2019. He made 838 runs at 27.93, with five fifties and a highest score of 93. That 93 is the sort of number a batsman remembers for a long time, and not always fondly.

White-ball cricket became his main stage. He made his first one-day hundred against the United Arab Emirates in Harare in 2018 and was named man of the match, and in 2019 he reached a century against England from just 82 balls, the fastest by a West Indies batsman against them in a one-day international.

What made him special

He batted to attack, and once he got going the ball tended to disappear. In 2018 the International Cricket Council picked him as one of five men who had broken through that year, and the following year it picked him out again as one to watch at the World Cup.

A Test hundred never quite arrived, though that 93 showed it was not far away. Bowlers in the shorter formats, who saw rather more of him, may have wished the selectors had kept him busier in whites.

Away from the middle

He became a sought-after player in leagues around the world, with the Royal Challengers Bangalore, the Delhi Capitals and the Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League, the Multan Sultans in Pakistan and the Khulna Tigers in Bangladesh. In 2018 he became the youngest batsman to make a century in the Caribbean Premier League, and in 2022 he captained the Guyana Amazon Warriors.

In the 2026 season of that league he made two hundreds, an unbeaten 111 from 43 balls and then a century from 45 balls in a qualifier, only the second man to manage two in one season. At the T20 World Cup earlier that year he hit 85 from 34 balls against Zimbabwe, the fastest fifty by a West Indian at a T20 World Cup.

And finally

Bowlers who saw his name on the team sheet learned to check the boundary riders were wide awake. On his good days, even that did not help much.
